correctness.rationale: The outer map is exactly the polynomial \(p(H)=(1-\alpha)I+\alpha(I-\eta H)^k\). The stability conditions follow by solving \(-1<p(\lambda)<1\) on positive curvature modes. The interval minimax proof is exhaustive: for even \(k\) interpolation cannot lower a subunit nonnegative power, while for odd \(k\) the fixed-\(\eta\) optimum is either \(\alpha=1\) or balanced endpoints; the auxiliary derivative argument proves both branches are bounded below by \(q^k\).

value.rationale: The theorem resolves the source paper's larger-inner-learning-rate motivation into an exact parity-dependent boundary, then shows that this extra stability is not equivalent to worst-case spectral acceleration. The distinction is structurally useful: odd \(k\) with \(\alpha<1\) can stabilize otherwise divergent inner steps, while the best fixed robust rate on a known SPD interval still turns interpolation off.
